sourcedFrom: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) (2026 (the cover prints Rev. 2026; no © line))
cleanIntro:
This guide follows Extar's owner's manual for its EP series pistols, which names the EP9. Every step below is quoted from that book.

The EP9 splits like an AR: the rear take down pin opens, the upper comes forward off the lower, the buffer and action spring come out, and the bolt comes out of the upper and is stripped of its firing pin and extractor. The book stops there and says to go no further into the bolt. It also says the pistol is built to run clean and dry, without oil.

steps.title: Safety on, with the hammer cocked
steps.action: Keep the pistol pointed in a safe direction for the whole procedure and put the selector on SAFE. The selector only reaches SAFE when the hammer is cocked, so if it will not turn, the hammer is down; do not force it.
steps.quote: Place your safety selector on “SAFE”. You cannot select the “SAFE” position unless the hammer is cocked.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Unloading and Clearing Your Pistol, step 2, p.6

steps.title: Magazine out
steps.action: Press the magazine catch button and take the magazine out of the well. Do this before touching the charging handle, or the bolt will feed a fresh round as it goes forward.
steps.quote: Depress the magazine catch button and remove the magazine.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Unloading and Clearing Your Pistol, step 3, p.6

steps.title: Charging handle back, chambered round out
steps.action: Pull the charging handle fully to the rear until it stops. Any round in the chamber is thrown out of the ejection port; let it drop rather than trying to catch it, and keep your fingers clear of the port.
steps.quote: Eject the chambered cartridge by retracting the charging handle until it stops. Let the ejected cartridge fall to the ground.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Unloading and Clearing Your Pistol, step 4, p.6

steps.title: Chamber and receiver looked into
steps.action: Hold the charging handle at the rear and look into the chamber and the receiver. Only when you see no cartridge anywhere in the action or the chamber, let the handle go forward and return the bolt to battery for disassembly.
steps.quote: While holding the charging handle to the rear, inspect the chamber and receiver to ensure you have removed any cartridges from the action and barrel chamber.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Unloading and Clearing Your Pistol, step 5, p.7

steps.title: Rear take down pin pushed partway from the left
steps.action: From the left side, push the rear take down pin just far enough that its detent no longer holds it closed. Use a bullet tip or a similar tool, then grip the head on the right side. The book says not to drive it out with a punch.
steps.quote: Partially push the rear take down pin from the left side so it is not captured by the detent that retains it in the receiver in the closed position.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Disassembly Instructions for Normal Cleaning and Maintenance, step 2, p.9
steps.warn: Do not attempt to drive it out with a punch.

steps.title: Pin pulled out to its open detent
steps.action: Pull the take down pin out to the right until it clicks into the detent that holds it open. It stays in the lower receiver; it does not come out completely.
steps.quote: Pull the rear take down pin the rest of the way to the right side of the lower receiver until it engages the detent that holds the pin in the open position.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Disassembly Instructions for Normal Cleaning and Maintenance, step 3, p.9

steps.title: Upper pushed forward off the front hook
steps.action: Hold the front of the magazine well with your thumb on the back of the hand guard retainer and push the upper forward. The back lifts loose as the front comes off its retaining hook, all in one movement. If it will not lift, check that the rear pin is fully at its open detent.
steps.aside: Grasp the front of the magazine well with a thumb up on the back of the hand guard retainer as shown in the illustration below.
steps.quote: Push the upper assembly forward with thumb until it lifts up in the back to a loose position and simultaneously disengages from the front retaining hook.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Disassembly Instructions for Normal Cleaning and Maintenance, step 4, p.10

steps.title: Upper and lower apart
steps.action: The upper and lower receiver groups are now separate. Set the upper aside; the lower comes next.
steps.quote: The upper and lower receiver groups are now separated; set the upper receiver group aside.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Disassembly Instructions for Normal Cleaning and Maintenance, step 5, p.10

steps.title: Buffer and action spring out of the lower
steps.action: Press the buffer slightly into the receiver extension tube and keep it pressed. The retaining plate in the slot of the lower can then be lifted out. The action spring is pushing on the buffer the whole time, so control it as it comes out. Holding the hammer down past the cocked position lets the buffer and spring slide out of the extension easily.
steps.aside: Holding the hammer depressed past the cocked position will allow the buffer and spring to be easily removed from receiver extension.
steps.quote: Remove the buffer and action spring from the lower receiver by first depressing the buffer slightly into the lower receiver extension tube.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Disassembly Instructions for Normal Cleaning and Maintenance, step 6, p.10
steps.warn: While removing, remember it will be under pressure from the action spring.

steps.title: Bolt assembly out of the upper
steps.action: Set the lower, buffer and spring aside and pick up the upper. Pull the charging handle back a couple of inches and draw the bolt assembly straight out of the back. Nothing else needs to be released.
steps.quote: Move the charging handle a couple of inches to rear and remove the bolt assembly. It will simply pull straight out with no further action required.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Disassembly Instructions for Normal Cleaning and Maintenance, step 8, p.11

steps.title: Firing pin retainer out from the left
steps.action: Push the firing pin retainer out of the left side of the bolt carrier group with a small tool. If it binds, press the firing pin in slightly to take the spring tension off the retainer.
steps.aside: To further aid disassembly you may need to slightly depress the firing pin to relieve tension from the firing pin spring.
steps.quote: Remove the firing pin retainer from the left side of the bolt carrier group.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Disassembly Instructions for Normal Cleaning and Maintenance, step 9, p.11

steps.title: Firing pin tipped out
steps.action: Tilt the bolt face up and let the firing pin come out of the bolt. Keep its spring with it; the spring has to go back on the pin a particular way.
steps.quote: Tilt bolt face up and remove firing pin from the bolt.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Disassembly Instructions for Normal Cleaning and Maintenance, step 10, p.11

steps.title: Extractor out by its retaining pin
steps.action: Press lightly on the side of the extractor and pull its retaining pin up and out of the bolt, then lift the extractor away. Note the pin's loop: it goes back in from the top, with the loop on top.
steps.aside: When reinserting the extractor retaining pin, you must insert it from the top, not the bottom. The loop must be on the top.
steps.quote: Remove the extractor by pulling the retaining pin up and out of the bolt while applying slight pressure onto the lateral face of the extractor.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Disassembly Instructions for Normal Cleaning and Maintenance, step 11, p.11

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Upper and lower are apart, the buffer and action spring are out, and the bolt is out with its firing pin and extractor removed. The book says this is as far as normal cleaning needs, and that the bolt goes no further.
steps.quote: Your pistol is now disassembled to the point necessary for normal required cleaning and maintenance.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Disassembly Instructions for Normal Cleaning and Maintenance, step 12, p.11
steps.warn: Do not attempt disassembly of your bolt any further than herein described.

steps.title: Cleaned with ordinary products
steps.action: Clean the parts with the cleaning products you would use on any firearm. The book says the EP9's components are not harmed by even strong solvents.
steps.aside: The EP9 components are impervious to even the most powerful solvents or hydrocarbons.
steps.quote: Cleaning is achieved with traditional products.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Disassembly Instructions for Normal Cleaning and Maintenance, step 13, p.11

steps.title: Left clean and dry, not oiled
steps.action: Leave the parts clean and dry. The book says the pistol is built not to need oil, and that oil tends to hold and spread dirt through the action.
steps.quote: Your EP series pistol will have optimal performance and best longevity if simply kept clean and dry.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Disassembly Instructions for Normal Cleaning and Maintenance, step 13, p.11

steps.title: If anything, a dry lubricant
steps.action: If you want to use a lubricant anyway, a light fog of silicone spray or a PTFE dry lubricant is better than oil. The book still says the pistol lasts longest with none at all.
steps.quote: If anything, “dry” lubricants such as a light fog of silicone spray or any of the PTFE based dry lubricant sprays are preferable over oil, but again, best longevity will be achieved without their use.
steps.cite: EP Series Pistol Owner's Manual — Rev. 2026 (printed on the cover) — Disassembly Instructions for Normal Cleaning and Maintenance, step 13, p.11

deepAbsentReason: The book has one disassembly procedure and it ends at the bolt. Removing the firing pin and extractor is already part of normal cleaning (steps 9 to 11, p.11), and step 12 forbids taking the bolt any further. There is nothing deeper to walk.

cleaning.name: CLEAN & DRY
tasks: Upper, lower, bolt, firing pin, extractor, buffer and spring cleaned with ordinary cleaning products
Every part left clean and dry
Do not oil the parts: the book says oil holds and spreads dirt and does not help this pistol

cleaning.name: LUBRICANT (OPTIONAL)
tasks: Only if you insist: a light fog of silicone spray or a PTFE dry lubricant, never oil
Best wear life is with no lubricant at all

reassembly: Assembly is the reverse order of the disassembly steps.
IMPORTANT: The firing pin spring, if it has been removed, must be assembled back onto the firing pin as illustrated with the spring all the way up over the retaining shoulder.
When reinserting the extractor retaining pin, you must insert it from the top, not the bottom. The loop must be on the top.
Upon reinserting the bolt into the upper receiver make sure that the last round bolt hold open actuator is positioned out of the path of the bolt.
Close the upper onto the lower at the front hook, push the rear take down pin back in from the right, then check the selector reaches SAFE with the hammer cocked.
fncheck: With the pistol confirmed empty and no magazine in it, retract the charging handle and let it go: the bolt should run fully home, and the selector should reach SAFE with the hammer cocked. The book warns that a firing pin spring not seated fully over its retaining shoulder can break the spring or pin and stop the pistol working, so a light or missing strike on the first rounds means stop and recheck it.
